newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares close lower despite partial recovery.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares close lower despite partial recovery.

text.p: Late buying by domestic financial institutions trimmed early losses as share prices on the Delhi Stock Exchange closed lower on Wednesday, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index ended 6.65 points lower at 740.97.
"The fall in share prices came to a halt once the domestic financial institutions started making purchases," said one broker.
Brokers said the market was unlikely to show any definite trend until the government presented the budget 1997/98 (April-March) on February 28.
"The market has turned highly volatile and it was difficult for the players to judge the future trend," said Sunil Prabhakar of brokers Spurt Securities.

Traders said heavy selling by speculators and foreign financial institutions, triggered by a standoff between India's Congress party and the ruling United Front government, had pushed down share prices in early trade.

On Sunday the Congress party issued a statement warning Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's centre-left coalition not to take its crucial support for granted, saying it would give its backing to the government on specific issues.
Deve Gowda's 13-party coalition depends on Congress to survive in parliament.
Reliance Industries closed 0.80 rupee lower at 271.45.
ACC closed 57.50 rupees higher at 1,476.50 on heavy institutional buying. The share had plunged to 1,350 rupees in early trade.
Bajaj Auto ended 26 rupees higher at 942.
State Bank of India ended 1.25 rupees lower at 288.
